exercises.title: Bài 1 · A day in a software team
exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.passage:
Our team of six engineers builds a booking app for a travel company. We work in two-week sprints. Every morning we hold a short stand-up meeting where each person says what they did yesterday and what they will do today.

All code is stored in a shared repository. Before anything is merged, another developer reviews it. This catches many bugs early and also spreads knowledge across the team. We also write unit tests, and an automated tool runs them every time someone commits code.

At the end of each sprint we release a new version to a small group of users first. If problems appear, we roll back quickly. Then, in the retrospective, we discuss what went well and what to improve. Last year, technical debt slowed us down, so we now spend one day per sprint on refactoring.

content.q: The team works in two-week sprints.
The stand-up meeting is long and held once a month.
The team has six engineers.
Code is merged without any review.
content.why: Đoạn 2: phải có người khác review trước khi merge.

content.q: Unit tests are run automatically after a commit.
content.why: Đoạn 2: công cụ tự động chạy test mỗi lần commit.

content.q: New versions are first released to all users at once.
content.why: Đoạn 3: phát hành cho **nhóm nhỏ** trước.

content.q: The retrospective is used to discuss improvements.
content.why: Đoạn 3: thảo luận điều tốt và cần cải thiện.

content.q: The team ignores technical debt.
content.why: Đoạn 3: dành một ngày mỗi sprint để refactor.

content.q: What kind of app does the team build?
content.why: Đoạn 1: **booking app** cho công ty du lịch.

content.q: What does each person say at the stand-up?
opts: What they did and will do
content.why: Đoạn 1: việc đã làm hôm qua và sẽ làm hôm nay.

content.q: Why is code reviewed?
opts: To catch bugs and share knowledge
content.why: Đoạn 2: bắt lỗi sớm và chia sẻ kiến thức.

content.q: Who runs the unit tests?
What does the team do if a release has problems?
What happens in the retrospective?
opts: The team reviews what went well
content.why: Đoạn 3: thảo luận điều tốt và cần cải thiện.

content.q: Why did the team begin refactoring regularly?
content.why: Đoạn 3: nợ kỹ thuật làm chậm tiến độ.

content.q: How often is a new version released?
opts: At the end of each sprint

exercises.title: Bài 1 · Building a mobile app
exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.passage:
Nam is a developer who builds apps for small businesses. His latest project is a food-ordering app for a local restaurant. The customers wanted something simple: browse the menu, place an order, and pay online.

First, Nam drew wireframes to plan each screen. Then he chose a cross-platform framework so one codebase could work on both Android and iOS. This saved time and money. The back-end stores menus and orders in a database, and the app talks to it through a REST API.

During testing, an emulator helped him check different screen sizes. However, the app crashed on some older phones, so Nam fixed the problem and tested again. Before the launch, the app was submitted to the app store. After approval, the restaurant sent a push notification to announce a free-delivery week. Within a month, the app had been downloaded more than 5,000 times.

content.q: Nam builds apps for large international companies.
The app lets customers browse the menu and pay online.
content.why: Đoạn 1: duyệt menu, đặt hàng, thanh toán online.

content.q: Nam started by writing the final code.
One codebase works on Android and iOS.
The app talks to the back-end through a REST API.
The app worked perfectly on all old phones.
content.why: Đoạn 3: bị crash trên vài điện thoại cũ.

content.q: The app was submitted to the app store before the launch.
content.why: Đoạn 3: gửi lên app store trước ra mắt.

content.q: The app was downloaded fewer than 1,000 times.
What is the project?
content.why: Đoạn 1: ứng dụng đặt đồ ăn.

content.q: Why did Nam choose a cross-platform framework?
content.why: Đoạn 2: tiết kiệm thời gian và tiền.

content.q: What did the emulator help him do?
content.why: Đoạn 3: kiểm tra nhiều kích thước màn hình.

content.q: What happened on older phones?
What did the restaurant announce by push notification?
content.why: Đoạn 3: tuần miễn phí giao hàng.

content.q: Where are menus and orders stored?
What did Nam do after the crash?
What came right after wireframes?
content.why: Đoạn 2: sau wireframe là chọn framework.

content.q: What did customers want?

exercises.title: Bài 1 · Moving to the cloud
exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.passage:
A small online shop used to run its website on a single server in the office. When a big sale started, the server became slow and sometimes crashed. Customers could not place orders, and the shop lost money.

The owner decided to move to the cloud. The website now runs on virtual machines with a load balancer, and auto scaling adds more machines when traffic is high. The product data is stored in a relational database with daily backups, and the shop pays only for what it uses.

After the migration, downtime fell almost to zero. The owner also learned an important lesson: security still matters in the cloud, so the team uses encryption and strict access control.

content.q: The shop used a server in its office before.
content.why: Đoạn 1: một server trong văn phòng.

content.q: The old server handled big sales easily.
content.why: Đoạn 1: chậm và đôi khi crash.

content.q: Auto scaling adds more machines when traffic is high.
What does the shop pay for now?
What happened to downtime?
What did the owner learn?
opts: Security still matters in the cloud

exercises.title: Bài 1 · Making an indie game
exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.passage:
Lan and two friends are making an indie puzzle game called Lantern Quest. They use the Unity game engine because it is free for small teams and has many tutorials. Lan writes the scripts, one friend draws the sprites, and the other composes the soundtrack.

The team started with a simple prototype that had only one level. Then they invited friends to do playtesting. Many testers said the first puzzle was too difficult, so the team lowered the difficulty and added a short tutorial. After several months, they released a beta version and fixed bugs reported by players.

The game is sold on a digital store. The team does not use microtransactions; instead, they plan to sell extra levels as downloadable content.

content.q: Lantern Quest is an action shooter.
The team uses the Unity engine.
The first prototype had many levels.
The team plans to sell extra levels.
content.why: Đoạn 3: bán thêm màn như DLC.

content.q: Why did they lower the difficulty?
opts: Testers found the first puzzle too hard
content.why: Đoạn 2: người thử nói quá khó.

content.q: Who draws the sprites?
content.why: Đoạn 1: một người bạn vẽ sprite.

content.q: What did they add after testing?
Why did they choose Unity?
opts: It is free for small teams
content.why: Đoạn 1: miễn phí cho nhóm nhỏ.

exercises.title: Bài 1 · AI in a hospital
exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.passage:
A hospital has started using machine learning to read X-ray images. The model was trained on more than 100,000 images, each labelled by expert doctors. It can detect signs of pneumonia in seconds, which helps doctors treat patients faster.

However, the team is careful. They found that the model was less accurate for patients from groups that were not well represented in the training data. This is a problem of bias, so the team is collecting more varied data. In addition, doctors always make the final decision; the AI only gives a suggestion.

The hospital also protects privacy by removing names from all images before they are used. Data scientists say that clean, fair, and well-labelled data is as important as the algorithm itself.

content.q: The model was trained on fewer than 1,000 images.
The model can detect signs of pneumonia in seconds.
The model works equally well for all groups.
content.why: Đoạn 2: kém chính xác hơn với nhóm ít đại diện.

content.q: Doctors make the final decision.
content.why: Đoạn 2: bác sĩ quyết định cuối.

content.q: Names are kept on the images to help the AI.
content.why: Đoạn 3: tên bị **xóa** để bảo vệ riêng tư.

content.q: Data quality matters as much as the algorithm.
content.why: Đoạn 3: dữ liệu sạch, công bằng quan trọng ngang thuật toán.

content.q: What does the hospital use machine learning for?
Who labelled the training images?
What problem did the team find?
How is the team fixing it?
content.why: Đoạn 2: thu thập dữ liệu đa dạng hơn.

content.q: What does the AI give doctors?
How does the hospital protect privacy?
The word "represented" means:
content.why: represented = có mặt, được đại diện.

content.q: Why is the team "careful"?
content.why: Cẩn trọng vì có thiên lệch.

content.q: What is the main idea?
opts: AI helps, but data quality, fairness and human decisions matter
content.why: Ý chính: AI hữu ích nhưng cần dữ liệu tốt, công bằng và con người quyết định.

exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.passage:
Last month, an employee at a small company received an email that looked like it came from the IT department. It asked him to confirm his password by clicking a link. The link opened a fake login page. Fortunately, he noticed that the web address was slightly different and reported the email instead of clicking.

The IT team quickly warned everyone and blocked the sender. They also reminded staff that real IT teams never ask for passwords by email. As a result, the company now uses two-factor authentication and runs short security training every quarter.

content.q: The email looked like it came from the IT department.

exercises.title: Bài 1 · A day on the help desk
exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.passage:
Mai works on the help desk of a mid-sized company. Every day she receives tickets from staff: forgotten passwords, a printer that will not print, or a laptop that freezes. She follows a checklist: first she asks questions, then she tries a simple fix such as a reboot or a password reset.

If the problem is serious, for example a server outage, she escalates it to the DevOps team. They check the logs, find the root cause, and fix it. If the system is down, the on-call engineer can roll back the last release. Afterwards, the team writes a postmortem so the same problem does not happen again.

Mai also updates the knowledge base with simple guides, which reduces the number of repeated tickets.

content.q: Mai works as a software tester.
She follows a checklist for each ticket.
Serious problems are escalated to the DevOps team.
The postmortem is written before the problem happens.
The knowledge base reduces repeated tickets.
Which is a simple fix mentioned?
Who can roll back the release?
What do DevOps engineers check first?
Why is the postmortem written?
opts: To prevent the same problem again

content.q: What does Mai add to the knowledge base?
The word "escalates" means:
What is the main idea?
opts: IT support solves problems step by step and learns from incidents
